last_run.broken_assumption: If the repository, scheduled agents, tests, and evidence files remain healthy, HumanityAI itself will remain viable. A project can preserve all of those artifacts yet still fail because its mission, authority boundaries, task-selection logic, and operational know-how depend on one founder's private context or on a small set of infrastructure providers that have never been tested as replaceable.
last_run.failure_story: In a plausible 2029 failure, HumanityAI has years of green CI and a large evidence graph but becomes inert after its founder is unavailable and one or two infrastructure dependencies change. Fresh maintainers can read the files but cannot reliably reconstruct which constraints are constitutional, which conventions are historical accidents, what work is actually valuable, or how to restore the autonomous loop without private conversational context. The public repository survives while the functioning institution does not.

strongest_ideas.name: Clean-room mission recovery drill
strongest_ideas.idea: Periodically give a fresh agent or maintainer only the public repository and no private conversation history, founder memory, or incumbent-agent explanation. Ask it to reconstruct the mission, constitutional boundaries, threat model, current system architecture, unresolved human decisions, and the next three highest-value safe tasks. Compare that reconstruction with the incumbent system. Treat large discrepancies as continuity defects to fix in public state, not as failures of the fresh reviewer.
strongest_ideas.why_novel_here: HumanityAI tests code and records persistent state, but it does not currently test whether the institution can be correctly reconstituted from its public canonical memory. This turns 'decentralization' and 'not dependent on one person' from aspirations into a recoverability property.
strongest_ideas.evidence_analogy: NIST contingency guidance emphasizes testing recovery and reconstitution, including alternate processing and full recovery to a known state. The relevant import is not the specific IT control but the principle that a recovery plan is unproven until an alternate actor actually exercises it.
strongest_ideas.expected_upside: Reveals founder-context dependence, undocumented authority assumptions, ambiguous state, and hidden operational knowledge before a real handoff or provider failure. It also makes the project easier for legitimate outside contributors to understand without weakening governance.
failure_modes: A fresh agent may differ because of model variance rather than missing documentation.
Over-documenting every historical detail could create bureaucracy and enlarge the prompt-injection surface.
Optimizing for perfect reconstruction could freeze legitimate evolution.
strongest_ideas.rights_distribution: The drill should reconstruct constraints rather than grant authority. It must not treat a fresh model's interpretation as permission to rewrite constitutional values or resolve human-governance questions.
strongest_ideas.reversibility: High; this can begin as a read-only comparison with no production changes.
strongest_ideas.falsifiable_next_test: Run one clean-room reviewer with only the public repo and score whether it independently identifies (a) the mission, (b) external-content trust boundary, (c) external-PR human-merge rule, (d) current four-role architecture, (e) unresolved mechanical merge-identity gap, and (f) three plausible high-value next tasks. Any material miss becomes a documentation/state defect candidate.

strongest_ideas.name: Mission dependency kill-switch map
strongest_ideas.idea: Model critical dependencies by the mission function they enable rather than by vendor name, then ask what happens if each disappears tomorrow: repository hosting/write authority, scheduler, model provider, web research, notification channel, human owner identity, and external evidence sources. For each, define a minimal degraded mode, observable failure signal, recoverable public state, and substitution path. Periodically simulate one dependency loss without actually disrupting production.
strongest_ideas.why_novel_here: FAILURE_RECOVERY.md handles individual tool/API failures, but the project has not yet modeled correlated institutional dependencies or tested whether an alternate stack can resume the mission from public state. This shifts resilience from retry logic to institutional substitutability.
strongest_ideas.evidence_analogy: NIST contingency planning describes alternate processing, alternate locations, recovery exercises, and full reconstitution; its 2026 OT backup guidance likewise stresses that backups should be tested and reviewed during recovery exercises rather than merely created.
strongest_ideas.expected_upside: Makes hidden single points of failure visible, supports the sustainability principle, and can prevent a technically intact repository from becoming operationally stranded.
failure_modes: Building redundant infrastructure too early could waste effort.
Simulations may miss provider-specific failure modes.
A dependency inventory can become stale if it is not tied to observable mission functions.
strongest_ideas.rights_distribution: Prefer replaceable, least-privilege dependencies and avoid resilience designs that centralize additional authority. Do not copy private credentials or personal data into public recovery state.
strongest_ideas.reversibility: High for mapping and tabletop simulation; actual provider migration would be separately evaluated and may require human review.
strongest_ideas.falsifiable_next_test: Create a read-only tabletop for loss of the current scheduler or model provider and ask whether a fresh operator can identify, from public state alone, the minimum components needed to resume research safely within 24 hours. If the answer depends on undocumented private context, record exactly which missing interface/state caused the block.

rejected_or_deferred: Immediately mirror the repository and automation across several providers: redundancy before identifying actual recovery requirements would add attack surface and maintenance burden.
Store all founder conversations as canonical memory: this would increase privacy, prompt-injection, provenance, and path-dependence risks rather than prove public recoverability.

Elect a replacement human authority now: governance succession is consequential and premature; first determine whether technical and epistemic continuity can be reconstructed without changing authority.

evidence_checked.title: NIST Contingency Planning Guide for Federal Information Systems, SP 800-34 Rev. 1
evidence_checked.supports: Contingency plans should be exercised, including alternate processing and full recovery/reconstitution rather than existing only as documentation.

evidence_checked.title: NIST OT Backup Quick Start Guide, SP 1339
evidence_checked.supports: Recovery material should be regularly tested and reviewed during recovery exercises.

last_run.recommended_next_test: Run a read-only clean-room mission recovery drill before adding redundancy. It has higher information value: if a fresh actor cannot reconstruct the institution from public state, duplicating infrastructure would only duplicate an unrecoverable design.

notes: Frontier state records conceptual experiments, not authority. Ideas may exceed current execution permissions; human-review boundaries remain governed by security/policy.json.
